name: aws-iam-authenticator-3642f9e5-blind29-ots
instr:
# aws-iam-authenticator: authentication and identity resolution give wrong answers, without a test suite

The repository has received 29 separate undocumented edits.

A deployment that lets cloud principals sign in to a cluster by presenting a signed credential, and that resolves each of them to a cluster username, a unique id and a group list, now answers wrongly in many places. Nothing about the protocol changed, nothing about the stored records changed, and nothing about the callers changed. Requests that used to be answered correctly come back wrong, and in several places a request that used to be served is refused outright.

Signing in. Posting a review request whose credential checks out, for a principal that has a stored record, comes back as a failure instead of the resolved username, unique id and groups, and it does so whatever source the record was loaded from. With only the source backed by the cluster's own stored objects in play, a principal whose object is present and already known locally is still treated as having no stored record at all, so those requests fail for a second, independent reason. With records supplied from a list on disk, a principal whose long canonical identity string carries capital letters is never lined up with the entry stored under the lowercased form of that string, so it signs in as unknown.
